input.quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Section 8 contains a one-way vendor indemnity in our favour: Commerce One must indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers against third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with a standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control to the vendor at its expense and counsel, cooperation at vendor's cost, plus a right for us to join with our own counsel). Exclusions are narrow and conventional (use other than as set out in the Documentation; modification by a party other than Commerce One where the infringement would not otherwise have occurred), and the remedy ladder is the usual procure / replace or modify / terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid. Section 9 expressly carves Section 8 out of both the 12-month fees cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, so the indemnity is uncapped — better for us than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. There is no Corio-side indemnity anywhere in the agreement, so the "narrow Customer indemnity" limb is satisfied by omission. The clause therefore meets the fallback (indeed exceeds it on the cap) and is compliant; no redline. Noted for the record only as sub-element gaps short of the preferred position: the indemnity does not extend to vendor breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data caused by the vendor, or vendor gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and the refund is tied to fees "paid" rather than "paid or payable". Given the uncapped IP indemnity and the absence of any reciprocal indemnity from us, these are not worth negotiating capital.
